comparison.rule: per quantity: |engine - source| <= atol + rtol * scale, with scale = |EFL| for the effective focal length and max(|BFL|, |EFL|) for the back focal length. atol = 0.005 mm is half a unit in the last decimal of the coarsest focal length these publications print (two decimals); rtol = 2e-3 is 1e-3 for a prescription printed to four decimals on radii as small as 0.27 mm plus 1e-3 for the engine's air-referenced index convention

materials.policy: Every glass is a constant index at the source's stated nd. A patent table gives nd and vd only, which cannot define a dispersion curve; fitting one would invent a material. Published catalog glasses were compared as a cross-check and are recorded under catalog_comparisons, never substituted.

catalog_comparisons.basis: cross-check only: the closest published glass by index; it is compared, never substituted, and the Project keeps the source's own nd

approximations.detail: the publication states this prescription in two states. TABLE 2 gives, for each, the object distance, the magnification and the three variable spacings: wide end object 10.4159 mm, variable 1 = 0.8375 mm, variable 2 = 0.2240 mm, variable 3 = 0.7827 mm, magnification -0.0910; telephoto end object 1.3910 mm, variable 1 = 0.1382 mm, variable 2 = 1.4271 mm, variable 3 = 0.2789 mm, magnification -0.8741. This record transcribes the wide end only, because the publication lists it first and it is the normal-viewing state the description calls the overview state. The telephoto state is not represented in the Project; it was built once as a scratch cross-check and its focal-length ratio is recorded under first_order.cross_checks
every glass is a constant index at the source's stated nd; the source's vd is recorded but no dispersion curve is modelled, so axial colour and chromatic focal shift are not represented
the Project is evaluated at the d line only

the source's tables for this example state no clear aperture, no F-number and no field angle, so the absolute scale of the apertures is not a source value. Every surface is edged to a uniform 0.39 mm clear semi-diameter (0.41 mm mechanical), which is the largest axial marginal-ray height of the design's own beam (0.341 mm at surface 10, with the stop opening at 0.297 mm) plus a 0.05 mm margin, read as a barrel. The stop opening, 0.2970 mm, is the value that keeps that margin, and it gives an image-space paraxial F-number of about 5.5; the source states no f-number, so none is claimed. The image-side plane-parallel plate (source surfaces 19-20) is edged to 0.70 mm because it is a 2.0832 mm long window in front of the image and its clear radius has to be positive and larger than the beam that reaches it. Semi-diameters set the solid checks only; they do not enter the first-order values

source surface 8 is an aperture stop at a zero spacing in front of surface 9. A zero thickness is refused by the format and a nominal gap would move the stop relative to the glass, so the stop is carried as surface 9's clear aperture (0.2970 mm), as this batch's import note prescribes. The opening is preserved; the opaque plate outside it is not modelled, so the record states STOP_NOT_BLOCKING
nominal prescription surfaces; no figure, centring or surface-roughness error is modelled
the three cemented interfaces (source surfaces 4, 14 and 17) are modelled as a shared surface between the two glasses; no cement thickness is stated and none is added

conversion.counts_note: the importer's 'elements' counts glass members; the source table's 20 surfaces form 11 glass elements, of which 3 are cemented pairs, grouped into 8 members

paraxial is NOT_CHECKED, not MATCHED: the publication states no effective focal length and no back focal length in millimetres for this example, so there is no source-stated first-order value to compare the engine's 1.002362 mm EFL and -0.083535 mm BFL against

the transcription of both states is nevertheless verified against the publication's own conditional expression (2): TABLE 6 states f_T/f_W = 1.431 for Example 1, and the engine gives 1.434457/1.002362 = 1.43108 when the telephoto column of TABLE 2 is built
the stated whole-system magnifications are reproduced to about 0.3 %: wide end -0.09127 against -0.0910, telephoto end -0.87722 against -0.8741
the object distance is the source's stated 10.4159 mm for the wide end, not infinity, so the Project is built for that finite conjugate
no aperture is stated by the source; the stop opening in the Project is derived and no f-number is claimed
